criteria.findings: The canonical author declaration and runtime/profile products require explicit finite read/write policies. Shared validation rejects duplicate or unsupported roles, engine-unreadable state and exposure contradictions. Task 2 independent fixture and pack review found no non-policy YAML deviations. No actor compatibility aliases/defaults or duplicate ScopedVariableRegistry return.

Ordinary get/set and global/agent convenience access require explicit actors; set_engine_value fixes engine identity and still authorizes. Qualified item reads/writes authorize and validate registered profile rows. Ordinary returned values are clones. Registry-owned frozen role snapshots resist later source declaration/profile mutations. Public access APIs have no permission bypass parameter.

Initialization/reset uses private lifecycle storage operations. VTC selects attempted destinations from action, active and condition masks before composition; same-value writes and failed claims remain attempts while nonselected entries do not. Commit preauthorizes all attempted VFS targets before transition bars, dones and registry writes. Static validation traverses typed nested command structures, maintains self versus retargeted loop namespaces and refuses known denied writes. Authored initial-state fields not admitted by current DTOs fail rather than silently bypass; dynamically constructed overrides are all authorized before allocation/registration. Compound command preflight conservatively checks nested targets before command mutation. Earlier independent commands are outside rollback scope. Loop preflight authorizes ordinary variable policies without resolving target rows or evaluating collection expressions. Inventory policy candidates are inspected deterministically by qualified profile. Actual loop execution resolves the collection once after earlier sibling state changes, authorizes the exact selected child contexts, then executes those contexts. No persistent cache or speculative branch RNG evaluation is introduced. The policy agent independently compared five actual bd34b538 parent controls against the repair, matching results and full RNG bytes.

Publication checks the registry-owned agent-read/exposure authority before constructing arena gather plans; mutable profile lists no longer filter bindings independently. Hidden and readable-unexposed declarations have no binding/payload. Persisted or constructed forbidden bindings refuse. The runtime batched gather path and token ABI remain intact, including row differences and qualified profile/liveness gates.

The committed pack has public, hidden, readable-unexposed and immutable variables. Actual ADVANCE actions change both public and hidden state; the named hidden reward changes by row while direct agent reads deny. Direct and serialized-cache variants cover two rows and two reset episodes. Qualified item probes use controlled actual spawning and explicitly avoid the initial item-appearance cache gap; they retain profile and despawn/liveness assertions.

Canonical identity tags ordinary ids and qualified (profile, variable) item ids separately, includes both permission sets even for hidden state, and sorts sets so role ordering is irrelevant. Existing four-term VFS composition is preserved. Artifact load requires current schema and policy fields, reconstructs and validates ordinary/profile policy coherence, token bindings and recomputed variable/VFS identity. Real serving and training resume tests refuse permission-only changes before applying weights, across flat and token brains.
